vsl.title: Another way to express ourselves. Another chance to understand.
vsl.body: A conversation can begin with movements of the hands, eye contact and facial expressions. Exploring VSL gives hearing people a chance to enter those conversations with initiative and respect.
vsl.note: VSL means Vietnamese Sign Language. Changing the interface language does not change the sign language being introduced.

beginning.title: We want to understand one another. But where do we begin?
beginning.one.title: Finding a clear learning source
beginning.one.body: With materials scattered across different sources, beginners need to know what to learn first and where to go next.
beginning.two.title: From watching to trying
beginning.two.body: Being able to watch a sign does not necessarily tell you whether your own attempt is appropriate.
beginning.three.title: Having a reason to keep going
beginning.three.body: A manageable path and opportunities to practise can help learning become a habit.
story.title: A wish to connect. A beginning for SignHearing.
story.one: We are building SignHearing as an approachable starting point for hearing people who want to learn VSL.
story.two: The project aims to organise learning materials by topic, helping learners watch sample videos and practise step by step. An AI feedback tool is being developed to support practice within a limited set of signs.
story.three: Each step in development needs to go hand in hand with reviewing content, listening to feedback and being clear about what the product can actually do.
journey.title: Building piece by piece, so every step of learning matters.
journey.body: SignHearing is currently building its foundation and preparing video learning materials. The planned curriculum includes 8 modules and 18 lessons, centred on familiar situations in everyday life.

meta.features.title: Explore SignHearing · Features & guides
meta.features.description: Explore SignHearing’s current tools through real screenshots and practical guides: roadmap, dictionary, videos, self-practice, review and progress.
features.hero.subtitle: Discover each feature and learn how to begin your Vietnamese Sign Language journey.

features.hero.index: tools to get to know, step by step
features.index.label: Choose a feature guide
features.showcase.eyebrow: From discovery to your own practice
features.showcase.title: Every tool. A little closer together.
features.showcase.body: Screenshots from the current development build. Materials labelled Sample have not been reviewed by VSL experts; official lessons are not open yet.
features.courses.title: Find your starting point.
features.courses.body: Explore the curriculum and choose an open lesson, at a pace that suits you.
features.courses.step1: Open Learning path in the learning space.
features.courses.step2: Choose Open to filter modules with accessible lessons.
features.courses.step3: Open sample Lesson 1 or Lesson 2 and select a sign from its list.
features.courses.step4: Read the meaning and observation prompts. Choose Mark as viewed, then move to the next sign.
features.courses.note: The two sample lessons currently have no videos. Lessons marked In preparation are not accessible.
features.courses.alt: Learning roadmap with the Open filter and two sample lessons in the first module.
features.courses.caption: Actual screenshot · Open filter selected, with no learning progress recorded.
features.library.title: One word. A new way to understand.
features.library.body: Look up a Vietnamese or English word, with or without accents, and explore its sign.
features.library.step1: Open Dictionary and enter a word in Find a sign.
features.library.step2: Filter by module, or choose Your video collection to find imported clips.
features.library.step3: Open a word card to see its meaning, content source and video when available.
features.library.step4: Choose Favorite on the detail page, then find it again with the Favorites filter.
features.library.note: Press / to focus search; Esc clears the query. Some signs do not have videos yet.
features.library.alt: Sign dictionary showing the search field, module filters and word cards.
features.library.caption: Actual screenshot · Sample signs and the imported video collection.
features.video.title: Watch. Pause. Take another look.
features.video.body: Watch a clip on its detail page, check its content status and continue into self-practice.
features.video.step1: In Dictionary, open a card labelled Video available · not reviewed.
features.video.step2: Use the video player’s play, pause and timeline controls.
features.video.step3: Read the notice beneath the video; choose Favorite to revisit the word later.
features.video.step4: Choose Self-practice to open the video beside the camera mirror, with speed and loop controls.
features.video.note: Imported clips are unreviewed and not assigned to curriculum lessons. English translations are provisional.
features.video.alt: Detail page for Ấm with the sample video player, content notice and Self-practice action.
features.video.caption: Actual screenshot · The sample “Ấm” clip is paused; this is unreviewed learning material.
features.camera.title: A little space to try for yourself.
features.camera.body: Put the reference video beside your camera mirror, compare for yourself and save your self-assessment.
features.camera.step1: Open a Self-practice session. Choose 0.5×, 0.75×, 1× or Loop video when a clip is available.
features.camera.step2: Choose Turn on camera and allow access to use the mirror, or use a physical mirror instead.
features.camera.step3: Compare handshape, location, palm orientation, movement and facial expression yourself.
features.camera.step4: Scroll down, check the items you feel you achieved and choose Save practice attempt; turn the camera off when finished.
features.camera.note: No video recording, audio recording or image uploads. This is self-assessment; AI grading is not available.
features.camera.alt: Self-practice session with the sample video, speed controls and the camera mirror switched off.
features.camera.caption: Actual screenshot · Camera off. No physical webcam or simulated camera was used.
features.review.title: Meet what you’ve learned, again.
features.review.body: Revisit signs with flashcards, then try a recognition quiz to record a result.
features.review.step1: Open Review; choose Viewed, Favorites or By lesson as your flashcard source.
features.review.step2: Choose Flip to answer to reveal the meaning, then Remembered or Not yet for this review session.
features.review.step3: Choose Take the quiz for an open lesson and answer its questions.
features.review.step4: Open the final result screen to save your score. At least 80% marks the lesson Completed.
features.review.note: Flashcard memory choices last only for the session. Lessons without videos use text-and-meaning quiz questions.
features.review.alt: Review page with By lesson selected, a sign flashcard and lesson quiz links.
features.review.caption: Actual screenshot · By lesson provides flashcards without fabricated progress.
features.progress.title: See the small steps add up.
features.progress.body: Find completed lessons, seen signs, practice sessions and quiz results in one place.
features.progress.step1: Open Progress in the learning-space navigation.
features.progress.step2: Check the four summary cards and the progress for each module.
features.progress.step3: Explore the 30-day activity calendar; Tab through its days for screen-reader details.
features.progress.step4: Scroll down to revisit saved self-practice, quiz results and seen signs.
features.progress.note: Progress is stored in your Supabase account and syncs across devices after sign-in.
features.progress.alt: Progress page in its first-visit state, with zero counters and an empty activity calendar.
features.progress.caption: Actual screenshot · A fresh browser profile with no activity; no illustrative achievements were added.

features.faq.eyebrow: A few useful things to know
features.faq.title: Before you begin.
features.faq.body: Short answers, grounded in how the current build works.
features.faq.account.q: Do I need to create an account?
features.faq.account.a: No. The current prototype opens directly and has no sign-in or account sync. You can explore its tools without registering.
features.faq.camera.q: Does the camera record or upload my image?
features.faq.camera.a: No. The camera starts only after your action, requests video without audio and works as a mirror. Turn it off at any time or use a physical mirror. Camera access requires localhost or HTTPS.
features.faq.ai.q: Can AI grade my signs yet?
features.faq.ai.a: Not yet. You assess the practice checklist yourself; quiz scores reflect recognition answers only. There is no AI feedback or movement-accuracy score.
features.faq.progress.a: In the Supabase database, linked to your account. Sign in with the same account on another device to restore progress.
features.faq.video.q: Why do some signs have no video?
features.faq.video.a: The two sample lessons have no approved videos. The separate collection of 12 imported clips is available in Dictionary and Self-practice, but is unreviewed and not assigned to the curriculum. Official learning materials are still being prepared.
features.faq.language.q: Does switching to English change the sign language?
features.faq.language.a: No. VI/EN changes the interface language only. The subject remains Vietnamese Sign Language; translations for the imported clip collection are provisional.
features.cta.eyebrow: A hello can open a connection
features.cta.title: The next step, at your own pace.
features.cta.body: Get to know the roadmap and try the current tools. Official lessons will open when the materials are ready and reviewed.
